resources.string: Pick your Budokai Tenkaichi 3 ISO (USA release, SLUS-21678). The app checks the image and unpacks the game data, like the PC port\'s setup. If you have no disc image, download one below.
From the project\'s own server, over Wi-Fi or mobile data. The image is deleted once the game data is unpacked.
This downloads 2.8 GB and needs about 3 GB of free space while it runs. On mobile data, that comes out of your data plan.
Levels, rewards and the season clock arrive with the first season.
Nothing to buy yet: the pass is drawn here so you can see what it will be.

This is not the unmodified USA release (a translation or a mod). Its files are used as they are, but the engine runs the original game program: what a mod changed in the game\'s code, rather than in its files, does not apply, and some mods may not work.
The files unpacked from the ISO will be deleted. Saves, textures and mods stay.
What carries your record to another phone or to the PC. Type it into the other device and both show the same record from then on. Keep it to yourself: it is that record\'s key.
Taken. This device now shows that record.
That is not a recovery code (32 letters a-f and digits).
The other player sees this in a match. Change it any time; it is kept.
Not included in this build. Everything you set up here (data, textures, mods, settings) is already where the engine will look for it.

The game\'s programs on this image do not have the expected checksums.\nThe unmodified USA release (SLUS-21678) is needed; a patched or damaged image will not work.

This zip does not look like a mod for the port: its folders must mirror gamedata/ (pzs3us0, pzs3us1, pzs3us2 or disc).
HD packs made for PCSX2 work as they are
Turns every pack on or off in the game without deleting anything.
Tap \"Add pack\" and pick the .zip. The app unpacks the textures (.dds or .png) into the right folder and the game uses them the next time it starts.
%1$s will be freed. To use it again, import the zip again.
Mods as .zip that replace game files, with folders as in gamedata (pzs3us0, pzs3us1, pzs3us2, disc). When two mods change the same file, the lower one wins.
Add .unk maps (the same ones used with PCSX2). They show up as new choices on the stage select.
Add .adx songs. They join the music (BGM) list with the name you choose.
Written with the game\'s own lettering on the select screen
Every character, stage, song and item, and maximum Zeni. It is the debug function the developers left in the game, the same one as in the PC port.
Will be applied the next time the game starts

The unlock is written to the game\'s save (memory card) and cannot be undone by the app. It is applied once, when the game starts, and the switch turns itself off again.\n\nPCSX2 cheats (.pnach) do not apply here: DBT3 runs the game\'s code natively, not an emulator.
The game\'s save will change the next time the game starts. Copy the saves folder if you want to keep your current progress.
They apply the next time the game starts
1x is the PS2\'s own resolution. On phones and handhelds, 2x or 3x is usually the sweet spot; on weaker GPUs (Mali, Adreno 6xx), try 1.25x to 1.75x.
FXAA smooths jagged edges. FSR and Snapdragon GSR upscale with sharper edges: best with an internal resolution below the screen\'s (1x to 2x), so they also help weaker GPUs.
The black line around the fighters
Shows a fighter hidden behind scenery
The haze that colours distant things
The bloom around bright things and the sky\'s glare
The soft focus on distant scenery
Automatic: they hide as soon as a physical controller is used (the Odin\'s own, a Bluetooth pad) and come back when you touch the screen.

The game computes a fight 30 times a second, as on the PS2; with this, pictures are drawn in between (frame interpolation), for 60 or 120 a second. The fight itself and online play are unchanged. It costs about twice the GPU work: for strong GPUs. Experimental: pictures are left out at camera cuts.
Screen: the phone\'s own shape, so the fight fills it. Wide shapes show more of the scene to the sides (nothing is stretched); the menus are drawn for 4:3 and are widened.

How finished pictures reach the screen. Automatic: Mailbox where the device has it. FIFO (VSync) waits for the screen\'s refresh: no tearing, a little more latency, steadier pacing on some devices. Mailbox: no tearing, no wait. Immediate: lowest latency, may tear. Used the next time the game starts.
Uses your wallpaper\'s colours instead of Goku\'s

Android port of Tenkaichi3Decomp, the native PC port of Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3 built on the BT3-Decompiled decompilation. Not affiliated with the game\'s developers, publishers or rights holders, and contains no game data: your own copy is needed.
The on-screen controller: when it shows, its look, its layout and macros
A short buzz when a button is pressed
The left stick starts where your thumb lands, anywhere on the lower left
Drag a control to move it. Tap it to select it: − and + resize it, α− and α+ adjust opacity, Hide hides it, Reset restores defaults. With nothing selected, size and opacity apply to all controls.
A macro is a button of your own on the screen that plays a sequence: a combo, or several buttons at once. Each step holds its buttons for a time; a step with no buttons is a pause.
Plays again for as long as the button is held (turbo)

For Snapdragon (Adreno) GPUs: another Vulkan driver, such as Turnip or a newer Qualcomm driver, from an AdrenoTools .zip. It can make the game start or run better where the phone\'s own driver fails. If the game does not start with it, choose System driver again.
That zip has no driver in it (.so)
If the game crashes or does not start: start it once, then come back here and save the log. It goes to Downloads, and you can send it straight away.

That link did not give a .zip file (it may be a web page).
This is a test build; it may be broken.
It installs over this version and keeps your game data, settings and saves. Open the app again afterwards.
Android needs your permission for DBT3 to install the update. Tap the button, turn on \"Allow from this source\", then come back: the update continues by itself.
Could not check for updates. Check the connection.
The downloaded file is not a DBT3 update.

In a clash of two beams or two rushes, tap or mash the Square (melee) button instead of turning the stick round. Works with the on-screen controls and with a physical controller. Also in the in-game window (Controls tab).

Game-specific: buttons for the game\'s own actions (target, Ki, melee, guard, dash…) in a thumb-friendly cluster, with a menu mode. Classic: the plain console pad (sticks, d-pad, four face buttons, shoulders). Each layout keeps its own placements.
Add a Play shortcut to the home screen
Creates an icon on the home screen that starts the game directly, without opening the app. The app icon\'s long-press menu has a Play entry too.
Shortcut requested: confirm it in the window that Android shows.
This launcher does not offer pinned shortcuts. Long-press the app icon: there is a Play entry.

Menu buttons in the menus and fight buttons in a fight, switched by itself. The MENU / FIGHT button on the screen still changes it by hand (for the pause menu in a fight, for example). Game-specific layout only.

Automatic: OpenGL ES on Mali GPUs, Vulkan on the others (Adreno runs Vulkan best). OpenGL ES (experimental) leaves out: depth clamping (what comes very near the camera can be cut off), the screen filters (FXAA, FSR, GSR); present mode FIFO is VSync on, the others off. If the chosen renderer cannot start, the game uses the other one. Takes effect the next time the game starts.
This zip uses a compression the app cannot read (Deflate64, LZMA, BZip2 or a password). Pack it again as a normal .zip (\"Deflate\", no password), for example with 7-Zip or ZArchiver.
